objective: Under G18, at the coordinator's go-ahead on the beyond-rejection referee's direction: map the preserved two-class sign (which starts have it, both knot laws, with and without symmetry, blow-ups) and ask whether any operation of ordinary growth or local reading counts the two classes with opposite weight; stop at such an operation with a frozen test or at an argument that growth treats the classes alike.
status: Complete 2026-11-26 (obstruction learned; referee pending): the preserved two-class sign is a parity-law property of the chosen moves (794 of 7,075 small starts; rings of 4-12 knots after one round; none under not-all-equal in what was read); on small starts the class is a single knot's value, on rings a whole cycle's parity (a classical code's sector); growth keeps every class at equal weight and nothing counts the classes with opposite weight.
title: The preserved two-class sign: where it is, and whether anything weights the classes oppositely
